definitions.explanation: Performing an action with full awareness and intent, as opposed to doing it by accident or mistake.

examples.japanese: {故意|こい}にやったのではない。
examples.english: I didn't do it on purpose.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{故意|こい}に{情報|じょうほう}を{隠|かく}していた。
{故意|こい}に{規則|きそく}に{違反|いはん}した{場合|ばあい}は、{厳|きび}しい{処分|しょぶん}が{科|か}せられる。
examples.english: If you deliberately violate the rules, severe penalties will be imposed.

notes:
A formal adverb used to express that an action was done on purpose. {故意|こい} is a noun meaning "intent, deliberateness" and に makes it adverbial. It is particularly common in legal, news, and formal written contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {故意|こい}に{壊|こわ}す — to break intentionally
- {故意|こい}に{無視|むし}する — to deliberately ignore
- {故意|こい}に{隠|かく}す — to intentionally conceal
- {故意|こい}に{遅|おく}らせる — to delay on purpose

SIMILAR WORDS:
- わざと — on purpose, deliberately (more colloquial; used in everyday speech)
- {意図的|いとてき}に — intentionally (similar formality; focuses on the planned nature)
- {意識的|いしきてき}に — consciously, intentionally (emphasizes awareness)

USAGE:
{故意|こい}に is more formal and written than わざと. In legal contexts, {故意|こい} (as a noun) contrasts with {過失|かしつ} (negligence): {故意|こい}による{犯罪|はんざい} (intentional crime) vs. {過失|かしつ}による{犯罪|はんざい} (crime by negligence).
